UK Motorcycle Touring Calendar

Plan your riding year with our month-by-month guide to the best UK touring destinations and conditions.

  • January–February: Winter maintenance and early season prep. Rating: 1/5.
  • March: Season opener rides, South Coast. 2/5.
  • April: Spring touring begins, Cotswolds. 3/5.
  • May: Peak District weekends, Isle of Man TT practice. 4/5.
  • June: TT Race Week, Scottish Highlands open. 5/5.
  • July: Peak season, NC500. 5/5.
  • August: Wales touring, Bank Holiday routes. 5/5.
  • September: Autumn colours, Yorkshire Dales. 4/5.
  • October: Last tours, Lake District. 3/5.
  • November: Night rides, South Coast. 2/5.
  • December: Winter riding, short day trips. 1/5.
keyTakeaways: The calendar rates each month from 1 to 5 for UK touring conditions.
June, July and August score the top 5/5 rating for peak-season riding.
June brings the Isle of Man TT race week and the Scottish Highlands opening up.
January and February score just 1/5 and are best used for maintenance and prep.
Autumn colours make September a strong 4/5 for the Yorkshire Dales.

comparisonTable.caption: UK touring conditions and highlights by month

faq.q: What is the best month for motorcycle touring in the UK?
faq.a: June, July and August score the top 5/5 rating thanks to the longest daylight, warmest weather and the widest range of open facilities. June is especially good, with the Isle of Man TT and the Scottish Highlands fully open. Just expect busier roads and popular routes, so ride early or midweek to beat the crowds.

faq.q: Is it worth riding in winter?
faq.a: January and February rate only 1/5, with cold, ice, salt-covered roads and short daylight making touring risky and uncomfortable. These months are best spent on maintenance and season prep. If you do ride, keep trips short and local, choose dry, milder days, and treat every shaded patch as potential ice.

faq.q: When should I plan a Scottish Highlands or NC500 trip?
faq.a: Aim for June to August, when the Highlands are fully open and the NC500 is at its best with long daylight and settled weather. Late spring and early autumn are quieter alternatives with fewer midges. Avoid winter, when remote roads, limited fuel and harsh weather make the far north genuinely hazardous.

faq.q: What can I do to prepare during the off-season?
faq.a: The 1/5 winter months are ideal for maintenance and planning. Service the bike, check tyres and battery, sort insurance and breakdown cover, and plan next year's routes. Getting these jobs done in January and February means you are ready to ride the moment conditions improve in the spring.

faq.q: Is autumn good for UK touring?
faq.a: September rates a strong 4/5, with spectacular autumn colours, fewer tourists after the schools return, and often settled weather, making the Yorkshire Dales and Lake District superb. October drops to 3/5 as days shorten and wet leaves appear. Enjoy the shoulder season, but watch for slippery leaves and early morning fog.
